name: Title

props.description: Sets BOTH the --heading-h{1..5} size token and the semantic <h1>..<h5>. Level 5 reads --heading-h5, which is bound to the existing --font-size-2xs step rather than being a new number. A value outside 1..5 falls back to h1, the way antd does — an <h7> from a runtime value would have no heading semantics at all. NOTE the default is antd's 1, while `Heading` defaults to 2.
props.name: level

props.description: Override the rendered element — a visual h2 that is a real <h1>.
props.name: as

props.description: Single-line ellipsis. `ellipsis` outranks it when both are passed.
props.name: truncate

props.description: Font weight, from the three-weight canon.
props.name: weight

props.description: Truncation. `true` is one line; `rows` clamps to N. `expandable` adds an expand control, `symbol` relabels it, `onEllipsis` fires when the measured overflow flips.
props.name: ellipsis
props.type: boolean | { rows, expandable, suffix, symbol, defaultExpanded, expanded, onExpand, onEllipsis, tooltip }

tagline: antd Typography.Title — a heading with five levels and the antd block behaviours (copyable, editable, ellipsis, the decorations). A SIBLING of `Heading`, which is this library's own four-level heading and is unchanged.
usage: DO use `Title` when you want antd's spelling, a fifth level, or a heading that is copyable / editable.
DO use `Heading` for everything else. It is the four-level heading the rest of this library is written in, and `CardTitle` / `PageContainer` already render one for you.
DON'T set `level` to pick a SIZE. It sets the semantic element too, so skipping from h1 to h4 for looks breaks the document outline — override the element with `as` instead.
useCases: A project name a user can rename in place: `<Title level={2} editable={{ onChange: rename }}>{name}</Title>`.
A dense sub-label below the body step, where `Heading` has no level left: `<Title level={5}>内訳</Title>`.
